content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 page triggered: west-us2 zone-b — significant increase in 5xxs from serving fleet. Routing scorecard shows egress failures to peering cluster gw-west-us2-b. Trace ID sample: 0a1b2c3d. Paging maria_oncall and carla_sre. Details: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/incidents/west-us2-egress.

maria_oncall: I'm on it. Seeing 5xx spike across model-serving pods in zone-b. Error = connection reset by peer to our egress gateway. Latency up ~2.1x for generation endpoints. Affected: hosted inference (text-gen), several dedicated pools in west-us2-zone-b.

carla_sre: Confirmed. Netflux graphs show packet drops on gw-west-us2-b at 2026-03-15T03:12Z. Cloud provider reports partial peering degradation to our transit. Opening ticket with provider now.

ben_ops: I'm preparing an immediate routing adjustment to divert traffic off zone-b. Plan: soft-divert2 policy -> route requests to west-us2-zone-a and fall back to west-us1 for heavy load. Will TTL shift for 5m, monitor, then increase if stable.

maria_oncall: Do not apply global scale-out to avoid double-sending customers. We only need routing shift at the edge. Also want to throttle some low-priority background eval jobs.

ben_ops: executing step: 
```
# internal routing CLI
rictl routes shift --from=west-us2-zone-b --to=west-us2-zone-a --policy=soft-divert2 --percent=70 --duration=5m --reason="egress gw failure"
```

ben_ops: shift started. Confirmed ~68% of traffic routed to zone-a. Monitoring error rate.

carla_sre: Provider update: peering fabric has high error rate on interface 3, they're rolling configs. ETA unknown.

emily_prod: Heads-up — Dedicated customers in zone-b may see increased latencies or intermittent failures. We should draft a short public status page and customer notification for affected dedicated customers and any Private deployments pointing at zone-b.

maria_oncall: Draft status page update (short): 
"We are investigating elevated errors for inference requests in west-us2 (zone B). Traffic has been temporarily routed to alternate zones. We will post updates as we have them. Impact: higher latency and intermittent failures for some requests. Mitigation steps: automated rerouting in progress. Next update in 15 minutes."

emily_prod: Looks good. Add timeframe: "Initial mitigation started at 03:18 UTC." Also add contact for customers with SLAs.

maria_oncall: Updated: 
"Initial mitigation started at 03:18 UTC. Customers with SLA concerns: support@redwood.ai or open a priority ticket."

maria_oncall: Draft customer email for Dedicated customers (short): 
"We are currently experiencing elevated errors affecting inference in west-us2 (zone B). Our operators have routed traffic to alternate zones to reduce errors; you may see higher latency or transient failures while we validate stability. We will follow up with a post-incident summary and any required remediation. If this impacts production SLAs, please contact the support team with priority."

dave_support: I'll queue the email to the dedicated-customer list and tag impacted accounts. Also preparing internal customer-impact table.

carla_sre: Quick mitigation status: soft-divert stable for 12m, 5xxs reduced by ~60% from peak but still above baseline. Packet drops persist on provider side; keep monitoring.

alice_eng: Noted a small number of model-serving pods in west-us2-zone-a showing increased memory pressure from the diverted load. Recommend scaling dedicated pools by +1 replica where safe and enabling batch-window tuning for latency-sensitive routes.

ben_ops: Scaling action (partial): 
```
kubectl scale deployment model-serving-pool-42 -n prod --replicas=3
kubectl annotate deployment model-serving-pool-42 redwood/ephemeral-scale=incident-2260007890
```
Scaling done for critical pools. Non-critical pools left at baseline.

maria_oncall: Running a quick sanity eval: sample generations across three models (small, base, large) — base model latency improved after shift but large model still has a 20% error rate for certain tokens. Hypothesis: KV cache warmup + quantization path mismatch on fallback hosts.

carla_sre: For large-model errors, we should enable fallback to compatible model-variant (quantized variant) to reduce errors. ben_ops, can you update routing rules for model-specific fallback?

ben_ops: Pushing model-level fallback rule now. 
```
rictl model-fallback add --model=redwood-large-v2 --from-zone=west-us2-zone-b --to-model=redwood-large-v2-q4_0 --condition=5xx > 10/min
```
Rule applied.

maria_oncall: Good. That reduced large-model error rate to ~8% in test queries. Monitoring production.

emily_prod: Preparing status page text (detailed): 
"What happened: we observed egress peering failures impacting west-us2 zone B which caused elevated 5xx and latency spikes for serving in that zone.
What we're doing: traffic has been temporarily diverted to west-us2 zone A and west-us1 while provider mitigates peering. We have applied model-level fallbacks for known large models and scaled critical serving pools.
Impact: customers with dedicated capacity in west-us2-zone-b and some hosted traffic may experience higher latency and transient failures.
Next update: in 15 minutes or after change of state."

carla_sre: Also add internal note: "Do not run broad cache invalidations during incident — only targeted warmup for scaled replicas."

maria_oncall: On-call handoff note (for next_oncall): 
"Summary: P1 - west-us2 zone B egress peering errors. Mitigations applied: soft-divert routing (70% -> zone-a), model-level fallbacks, scale critical pools. Current status: error rates down ~60% but not back to baseline; provider still has degraded interface. Open tasks: 1) Monitor error rate and latency for 1h, 2) escalate to provider CSE if no improvement in 30m, 3) prepare postmortem template and customer-facing timeline. See runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/incidents/west-us2-egress for all commands used.
Actions for next_oncall: confirm provider fix or continue divert, coordinate final status page update, run post-incident regression evals on quality metrics once traffic returns to zone-b."

next_oncall: Taking over. I'll set a 1h check-in and will update status page at that point. If provider doesn't clear, I'll prepare cross-region capacity increase options.

dave_support: Customer impact table (snippet): 
"
- Account: AcmeCorp — Dedicated pool in zone-b — Impact: increased latency, transient 5xx — Notified: yes (03:25 UTC)
- Account: BetaApps — Hosted usage — Impact: intermittent errors for large-model calls — Notified: no (monitoring)
"
I'll notify beta accounts if errors stay elevated after next update.

emily_prod: Suggested SLA message to customers: 
"We recognize this incident may affect your service-level expectations. We will include a timeline and root cause analysis in the post-incident report and will reach out directly to customers whose SLAs may have been breached."

maria_oncall: Logging final immediate mitigation state before handoff: 
"soft-divert active (70% to zone-a), model-fallbacks applied for redwood-large-v2, scaled 2 critical pools, provider ticket #PR-78932 open, next internal update scheduled at 03:45 UTC." 

carla_sre: Adding a quick internal comms blurb for the #general channel: 
"Heads-up: We've mitigated an egress peering issue in west-us2 zone B by diverting traffic; customer-facing status page updated. Expect some latency increases for affected workloads. Ops teams: avoid broad config churn until clearance."

maria_oncall: handing off to next_oncall now. If anything flares, page me and I'll jump back in. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident timeline note created and assigned to maria_oncall for postmortem.

next_oncall: Acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring and will publish the 1h follow-up.
